title: FastAPI for AI apps
summary: Wrap your AI logic in a FastAPI web service so other apps can call your model over HTTP.
objectives: Understand what a web API is and why AI apps need one
Build a FastAPI app with a POST endpoint

Read auto-generated docs at the /docs page

quiz.q: What does an API let you do?
options: Let one program call another over HTTP
quiz.why: An A P I (Application Programming Interface) lets programs talk to each other — here, a client sends a request and your server returns a response over HTTP.

quiz.q: Which decorator defines a POST endpoint in FastAPI?
quiz.why: @app.post("/path") registers a function to handle POST requests, which is the right verb for sending data like a prompt.

quiz.q: What is Pydantic used for in FastAPI?
options: Validating and parsing request and response data
quiz.why: A Pydantic BaseModel declares the shape of your data; FastAPI uses it to validate incoming JSON and document the schema automatically.

quiz.answer: In an environment variable, not hard-coded in the source.
quiz.why: Hard-coding secrets risks leaking them in Git. The Anthropic client reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the environment by default.

quiz.q: What command runs a FastAPI app named app in main.py during development?
quiz.why: Uvicorn is the A S G I server; main:app points to the app object in main.py, and --reload restarts on code changes.

quiz.q: What URL shows FastAPI's auto-generated interactive docs?
quiz.why: FastAPI serves interactive Swagger U I at /docs out of the box, generated from your Pydantic models and endpoints.

body_markdown:
## Why AI apps need an API

You have working A I logic — a function that takes a prompt and returns a Claude response. But a function only runs inside one Python process. To let a website, a mobile app, or a teammate use it, you expose it as a **web API**: a server that listens for HTTP requests and returns answers.

**FastAPI** is a modern Python framework that makes this fast to build, automatically validates your data, and generates interactive docs for free.

## Your first endpoint

An **endpoint** is a URL plus an HTTP verb that runs a function. For sending data like a prompt we use **POST**. The `@app.post` decorator wires a path to a handler.

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/health")
def health():
    return {"status": "ok"}
```

Run it locally with uvicorn, the A S G I server:

```bash
pip install fastapi uvicorn anthropic
uvicorn main:app --reload
```

## Validating data with Pydantic

Never trust raw input. A **Pydantic** `BaseModel` declares exactly what fields you expect and their types. FastAPI parses the incoming JSON into that model, rejects bad requests with a clear error, and documents the schema automatically.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel

class ChatRequest(BaseModel):
    prompt: str

class ChatResponse(BaseModel):
    reply: str
```

## Calling Claude from an endpoint

Inside the handler, create an Anthropic client and call the **Messages API**. The client reads `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the environment — keep keys out of your code.

```python
import os
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic()  # reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

@app.post("/chat", response_model=ChatResponse)
def chat(req: ChatRequest):
    msg = client.messages.create(
        model="claude-sonnet-4-6",
        max_tokens=1024,
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": req.prompt}],
    )
    return ChatResponse(reply=msg.content[0].text)
```

## Testing and docs

With the server running, open `http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs`. FastAPI generates an interactive Swagger page from your models — you can send a real request from the browser. Set your key first:

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
```

## Your task

Build a small FastAPI service with a `/chat` POST endpoint that calls Claude, validate the request with a Pydantic model, and test it from the `/docs` page.

slides.title: FastAPI for AI apps
slides.narration: Welcome to Month Four, where we turn your skills into portfolio projects. In this lesson we'll take your A I logic and wrap it in a web service using FastAPI. By the end you'll have a real A P I that other apps can call to talk to Claude over the internet.

slides.title: Why AI apps need an API
bullets: A Python function runs in one process only.
An A P I lets other apps call your model.
Clients send requests; your server replies.
slides.narration: So far your A I logic lives inside one Python program. But a website or a teammate can't reach a function on your laptop. An A P I solves this. It's a server that listens for requests over HTTP and sends back answers. That's how every real A I app, from chatbots to search, is built.

slides.title: Why FastAPI
bullets: Modern, fast Python web framework.
Validates your data automatically.
Generates interactive docs for free.
slides.narration: We'll use FastAPI because it's built for exactly this. It's quick to write, it checks your incoming data for you, and it generates a live documentation page automatically. That combination makes it perfect for A I services and a great thing to show in your portfolio.

slides.title: Your first endpoint
bullets: An endpoint is a U R L plus an HTTP verb.
Use POST to send data like a prompt.
@app.post wires a path to a function.
slides.narration: Let's build our first endpoint. An endpoint is a U R L paired with an HTTP verb that runs a function. Here we create the app, then use the get decorator to add a health check at slash health. When someone visits that path, FastAPI runs the function and returns the dictionary as Jason.

slides.title: Run it locally
bullets: Install fastapi, uvicorn, and anthropic.
Uvicorn is the A S G I server.
--reload restarts on code changes.
slides.code:
pip install fastapi uvicorn anthropic
uvicorn main:app --reload
slides.narration: To run the server we use uvicorn, which is an A S G I server. The phrase main colon app means the app object inside the file main dot p y. The reload flag restarts the server every time you save, which is perfect while you're developing. Now your A P I is live on your machine.

slides.title: Validate with Pydantic
bullets: Never trust raw input.
A BaseModel declares expected fields and types.
FastAPI rejects bad requests automatically.
slides.narration: Real apps receive messy or malicious data, so we validate it. A Pydantic base model declares exactly which fields you expect and their types. Here a chat request must contain a prompt that's a string. FastAPI parses the incoming Jason into this model and returns a clear error if anything's wrong.

slides.title: Call Claude in the endpoint
bullets: Create an Anthropic client.
Use the Messages A P I, not completions.
Return the text in your response model.
slides.narration: Now the heart of it. Inside the handler we call the Anthropic Messages A P I. We pass a model id like claude sonnet four six, a max tokens limit, and the user's prompt in the messages list. The reply text comes back in message dot content, and we wrap it in our response model so the output shape is guaranteed.

slides.title: Keep your key safe
bullets: Never hard-code secrets in source.
Store the key in an environment variable.
The client reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for you.
slides.code:
import os
from anthropic import Anthropic

client = Anthropic()  # reads the env var
slides.narration: One rule you must never break: don't put your A P I key in your code. If it lands in Git, it can leak. Instead store it in an environment variable called ANTHROPIC underscore A P I underscore KEY. The Anthropic client reads that automatically, so calling Anthropic with no arguments just works.

slides.title: Test from the docs page
bullets: Set your key in the shell first.
Open slash docs in the browser.
Send a real request from Swagger U I.
slides.narration: Time to test. First export your key in the terminal so the server can see it. Then open slash docs in your browser. FastAPI builds an interactive Swagger page from your models, where you can type a prompt and fire a real request to Claude without writing any client code. It feels like magic the first time.

slides.title: Common mistakes
bullets: Using GET instead of POST for sending data.
Hard-coding the A P I key.
Forgetting max_tokens in the call.
Returning data that breaks the response model.
slides.narration: Let's flag the traps. One: using get when you should use post to send a prompt. Two: hard-coding your key instead of using the environment. Three: forgetting max tokens, which the Messages A P I requires. And four: returning data that doesn't match your response model, which FastAPI will reject. Avoid these and you're solid.
